answer_en: Malaria is treated with ACT (Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy), available free at government health centres. See a health worker immediately if you have fever, chills, or headache, especially for children under five.
answer_lg: Omusujja gw'ensiri gujjanjabibwa n'eddagala erya ACT, eriweebwa obwereere mu bifo by'obujjanjabi ebya gavumenti. Laba omusawo amangu bw'obeera n'omusujja, okukankana, oba omutwe oluvannyuma.

answer_en: Pregnant women should attend at least 4 antenatal care visits at a health facility. Warning signs needing urgent care include heavy bleeding, severe headache, and reduced fetal movement.
answer_lg: Abakyala abali embuto balina okugenda mu bujjanjabi obw'olubuto obwa wiiki (antenatal) emirundi ennya nga tebannazaala. Bw'oba olina omusaayi omungi, omutwe ogw'amaanyi, oba omwana teyeetambuza, genda mangu mu ddwaliro.

answer_en: Children should receive vaccines according to the Uganda immunization schedule, starting at birth (BCG, OPV) through 18 months. Vaccines are free at all government health facilities.
answer_lg: Abaana balina okuweebwa akasago okusinziira ku puloguramu ya Uganda okuva lwe bazaalibwa (BCG, OPV) okutuuka ku myezi 18. Obukasa buweebwa obwereere mu ddwaliro lyonna erya gavumenti.

answer_en: The nearest government health facility can be found using the Ministry of Health facility locator, or by asking your local Village Health Team member.
answer_lg: Ddwaliro erisembera eritongole mu gavumenti oyinza okuliraba nga okozesa akasengejja k'ebifo by'obujjanjabi, oba nga obuuza omukugu wa Village Health Team ali okumpi naawe.
